name: Life-and-Death and Soul Sea Realms
reason: Compound sentence fragment joining two realm names ('Life-and-Death Realm' and 'Soul Sea Realm'), each of which is covered as its own entity.

name: Radiant Light Sect
reason: The source's 'Zhao Wu secret religion', a covert faith-recruiting cult, was renamed 'Radiant Light Sect' to fit the Western fantasy register and evoke a proselytizing religious order.
description: A secret human sect operating in Auspice City that gathers believers and accumulates Faith Energy, one of several such covert faiths. Its reserves were robbed (Ep 1126), to the quiet delight of its rivals.

name: Nether Water
reason: Source term 'Nether Yin Water' was simplified to 'Nether Water' for the Western fantasy setting, dropping the untranslatable 'Yin' qualifier.
description: A sinister dark water in which Cannibal Moth eggs lie dormant for tens of thousands of years; when prey approaches, the water drips outward and each falling drop hatches into a black moth charged with the rare Dark Law (Ep 1135).

name: Spirit Index
reason: The source's 'Universal Myriad Spirit Stele', the stele on which the names of supreme weapons appear, was condensed to 'Spirit Index' as a cleaner English concept for a ranked registry.
description: A mystical registry on which the names of supreme spirit weapons manifest of their own accord. Lavender and the Cobalt Dragon speculate whether a name connected to Zane will actually appear on it (Ep 1087).

name: Three Queens
reason: The source's 'three Kings' of the demon night clan are women, so the title was localized as 'Three Queens' to match their gender in English and avoid confusion.
description: The three ruling Queens of the demon night clan (including the Queen of Punishment), whose statues gather the faith power of millions; invoking the Power of the Three Queens can match far stronger beings. A bloodline awakening triggered this power without Lavender's intent, forcing the Queen of Punishment's hand (Eps 1157-1161).

name: Cosmic Order
issues: Split localization: the same source concept 'Heavenly Dao' is rendered 'Heavenly Way' in earlier episodes (~718-881) but 'Cosmic Order' in later episodes (1182+).
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Dao', the supreme law governing the universe, was localized as 'Cosmic Order' in the late episodes to convey a universal system of law without Daoist terminology.
description: The supreme system of laws governing everything from grains of sand to stars; inherited Celestial Laws such as the Eyes of Rebirth draw directly on it, and the Illusion Battlefield is said to be its projection. Gus is noted to have surpassed the Cosmic Order itself (Ep 1205).

name: Supreme Lords’
reason: Possessive plural fragment of the generic rank/title 'Supreme Lord'; not a distinct entity.

name: Dragon-Taming Sentinels
reason: The source's Buddhist 'Tiger-subduing Arhats' guardian statues were renamed 'Dragon-Taming Sentinels', swapping the Buddhist arhat/tiger imagery for dragon-themed guardians consistent with the show's register.
description: Four indestructible guardian constructs in the final chamber of a trial site; they shatter and re-form endlessly, and the Warden declares they cannot be destroyed (Eps 1220-1222).

name: Kincaid
reason: The source's 'Ji Family' clan was localized with the Western surname 'Kincaid' to create a consistent Western family unit for its members in the Illusion Battlefield arc.
description: A vast warrior family of the Upper Realm: over a million warriors bear the Kincaid name, rivaling a nation in size. Its reclusive patriarch came out of seclusion just to watch the Illusion Battlefield (Ep 1239).

name: Myriad Manifestations of Nature
reason: The source text 'Ten Thousand Wonders' was expanded to 'Myriad Manifestations of Nature' to read as the title of an arcane compendium in English.
description: An old text collecting the essays of Zane's Master, containing thousands of minor entries including the instructions for the Blood Refinement Technique (Ep 1234).

name: Blood Refinement Technique
reason: Near-literal rendering of the source 'Blood Refining Technique', lightly smoothed to 'Blood Refinement Technique' for English flow.
description: A refining technique recorded in the Myriad Manifestations of Nature, used in the source for collecting the Divine Essencefused Mountain; Zane considers it minor enough that he might have taught it for free (Ep 1234).

name: World Tree Venom Bugs
reason: The source's 'Amberwood Voodoo Parasites' were renamed 'World Tree Venom Bugs' to tie the creatures to the adaptation's tree lore and avoid the voodoo connotation.
description: Highly poisonous but easily lured insect creatures encountered in the Illusion Battlefield's withered-wood region (Eps 1246-1247); in the source Luo Zheng baits them without fear of their venom.

name: Halls of Causality
reason: Source organization 'Karma Hall' was localized as 'Halls of Causality', trading the Buddhist loanword 'karma' for its Western philosophical equivalent.
description: A powerful organization of the late arcs; Slade and his companions belong to it, eight of whom watch his fight near the city wall with grim concern (Ep 1312).

name: Hayden
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yu Han' was fully localized to 'Hayden', a name echoing the cool, austere sound of the original while fitting the Western setting.
description: A female True God of the 'Golden Generation' who was imprisoned in a river of ice for 100,000 years, comprehended the Godly Way of Snow (source: Snow Seal Divine Dao) and earned her Godly Sigil. She tests Zane's compatibility with her path and finds him unsuited (Eps 1299-1300).

name: Sealed Emotion
reason: The source's 'Severing of Emotions Divine Dao' was localized as the 'Divine Path of Sealed Emotion' / 'Sealed Emotion', softening the literal 'severing' into 'sealed' for English idiom.
description: A powerful but forbidden Godly Way in which the practitioner's emotions are sealed away; it was the path Zane's sword found for him rather than a deliberate choice, and even the True God Reggie speaks of it with wariness (Eps 1301-1312). The male pronoun signal near the name belongs to its practitioners, not the path itself.

name: Reggie
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mo Chen' was fully localized to 'Reggie', a punchy, brash-sounding name fitting the domineering saber-wielding True God.
description: A True God of the saber who pursued dominance his whole life, mastered the Domineering Divine Path and earned the Unrivaled Godly Sigil. Brash and fearless, he counsels Zane that the Path of Sealed Emotion is forbidden and doomed to waste his time (Eps 1301-1302).

name: Clark
reason: An unnamed armored soldier from the source's Holy City arrival scene was given the US-style name 'Clark' to carry dialogue in the adaptation.
description: An armored warrior in the Holy City who, together with Hawthorne, coldly warns the merchant Rylan to stay away from Zane, noting that Zane adjusted to the Vitality Pressure within seconds of ascending (Eps 1023-1025).

name: Alice
reason: An adaptation-added slice-of-life character; 'Alice Bishop' is a plain US name chosen to mark her as an ordinary, non-cultivating girl.
description: The innkeeper's young daughter, a normal person with no cultivation, who secretly witnessed the agony of Zane's Body Refining and brought him tea, watching with childish wonder rather than fear (Eps 477-478).

name: Heavenly Feather Crown
reason: The source treasure 'Heavenly Feather Saint Crown' of Beiyou Palace was trimmed to 'Heavenly Feather Crown', with its origin relocated to the Serenity Palace of the Arctic Lands.
description: A small golden crown from the Serenity Palace of the Arctic Lands, set with three uncut white crystals and three feathers, a high-grade (Relic-Class) weapon despite being an accessory. Eden offered it to Tia during the betrothal-gift contest (Eps 492-494).

name: Violet Power Domain
reason: The source technique 'Extreme Violet Domain' (Si Miaoling's purple true-essence domain) was localized as 'Violet Power Domain' for a clearer English power-fantasy ring.
description: Marilyn's trump-card domain technique: her purple energy floods the entire arena like a violet ocean, trapping her opponent inside where ordinary techniques prove worthless (Eps 510-512).

name: Thunder's Wrath
reason: The source formation 'Fury of Thunder Punishment' was tightened to 'Thunder's Wrath' for a punchier English name.
description: A lightning killing formation deployed by the Cloud Hall in tandem with the Madness Trap (source: Chaos Trap) against Maddox; victims caught in the illusion would be struck directly by its lightning, though Maddox sensed the killing intent and escaped (Ep 529).

name: Roland
reason: A Divine Kingdom elder from the source's cursed-Saintess arc was given the dignified Western name 'Roland' befitting his composed, senior-statesman role.
description: A composed elder of a Divine Kingdom attending the cursed Holy Maiden; he negotiates with Zane over the reward for lifting her curse, even offering a sect-protecting array on the Kingdom's behalf (Eps 543-546).

name: Demonic Dragon
reason: Near-literal rendering of the source 'Demon Dragon' as 'Demonic Dragon' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The dragon-and-snake apparition bound to the Divine Kingdom Prince, whose appearance horrifies Elder Imogen (source: Granny Yu); Zane senses a strange bloodline connection between himself and the beast (Ep 548).

name: Sages
reason: Generic plural of the rank 'Sage'; the specific pair referenced in these episodes is covered by the fuller entity 'Ogre Sages' from the Tower of Sin arc.

name: Black Nether Beads
reason: The source's 'Abyssal Beads' from the Profound Nether Cave arc were renamed 'Black Nether Beads', folding the cave's 'Nether' theme into the item name.
description: A pair of rare dark beads recovered from the Profound Nether Cave expedition; Esther Sterling (source: Ling Yan) presented them to Lavender, to the envy of Fabian and the others (Eps 643-644).

name: Frost Wolves
reason: The source's 'Azure Wolves' monster pack was recolored to 'Frost Wolves' for the Western fantasy register.
description: Powerful wolf monsters nesting on one side of a dangerous pass, opposite the Shadow-maw birds (source: Azure Wolves and Tuna Birds at the Bloody Mouth Pass); their guttural howls turn to frightened yelps when a greater power appears (Eps 645-677).

name: Elder Shaw
reason: The source's Sect Master Xiao of the Fish Dragon Sect was localized as 'Elder Shaw', with the surname 'Shaw' chosen as a phonetic echo of 'Xiao'.
description: The head of a sect (source: Fish Dragon Sect) who courts Zane warmly after the Immortal Tomb arc, scolding Master Young over mishandled reports and staying all smiles at Zane's side. Though he knows Zane is only at the Spirit-Tribulation Realm, he is keenly aware of Zane's relationship with Tia (Eps 687-773).

name: Lady Cora
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xi Youqin' was fully localized; 'Cora' with the honorific 'Lady' conveys her status as a noble house's sought-after young lady.
description: The young lady of a powerful house whose hand in marriage draws crowds of competing suitors (Ep 692, mirroring the source's Xi Family husband-selection for Xi Youqin); she later keeps secluded quarters that only she and a few handmaidens may enter (Ep 933).

name: Heavenly Way
issues: Split localization: source 'Heavenly Dao' appears as 'Heavenly Way' in Eps ~718-881 but as 'Cosmic Order' in Eps 1182+; the two localized names denote the same source concept.
reason: Near-literal rendering of the source 'Heavenly Dao' as 'Heavenly Way' in the mid-range episodes.
description: The governing law of the world; Lavender identifies a mysterious fragment as belonging not to the current Heavenly Way but to a previous one that existed long before it (Ep 718).

name: Melody City
reason: The source's 'Tian Yun City' was localized as 'Melody City', translating the 'Yun' (rhyme/melody) element of the Chinese name.
description: A small city where the Corrupted Divine Kingdom was secretly building a teleportation array; Zane and Finn's mission was to destroy it (Eps 738-759).

name: Octogram Mirror
reason: The source's 'Eight Trigrams Mirror' was renamed 'Octogram Mirror', replacing the I Ching trigram reference with a neutral eight-sided figure.
description: A mirror treasure through which a distant master can project a wisp of soul to communicate and spy; Zane keeps it in his Storage Ring and later regrets breaking it when its owner goes silent for a month (Eps 759-773).

name: Flames of Rebirth
reason: The source's 'Nirvana Flame', explicitly also called the 'Flame of Rebirth', was localized under that second name to avoid the Buddhist loanword.
description: The fourth level of the Law of Fire, releasable only by a phoenix during its moment of rebirth and the most devastating power in its arsenal. Zane walked through the Flames of Rebirth unharmed and used them to temper his body into a living weapon as hard as a Relic (Eps 821-823).

name: Feather Emperor's Secret Land
reason: Near-literal rendering of the source 'Feather Emperor's Secret Realm', with 'Realm' softened to 'Land' to avoid clashing with the show's cultivation-realm terminology.
description: One of the island secret realms opened with the Sacred Sea, left for the younger generation to explore; the only way in leads through the Spirit Beast Area to an entrance at the island's center, and the group refuses to miss their one shot at entering (Eps 840-845).

name: Master Priest
reason: The source's 'White Eyebrows Taoist' (addressed as 'Supervisor' at the tribulation site) was localized as the 'Master Priest', replacing the Daoist epithet with a Western clerical title.
description: The white-haired priest supervising the tribulation grounds, addressed deferentially as 'Master Priest' by the gathered warriors. He goes still on learning Zane is a saint-level genius of the Harlen Divine Kingdom, and the Demi-Immortal Race appears to hold a grudge against him and the Holy Maiden (Eps 880-954).

name: Emperor’s Isle
reason: The source's 'Divine Emperor Island' was shortened to 'Emperor's Isle' for a cleaner English place name.
description: An island that is less a home for the living than one massive black cemetery for the dead (Ep 904, mirroring the source's Divine Emperor Island graveyard). Even Soul Sea Realm masters refuse to fight over it, since a true battle between them would obliterate the entire isle in moments (Eps 890-926).
